findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkbox tasks instead of plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The commit points are at lines 71, 94, 117, 126 and 134. Each is written as a checkbox item, for example `- [ ] **Task 2C: Commit** — feat(core): ...`. Commit markers should be plain lines in the form `**Commit**: feat(core): add slice design heading validator`, never checkboxes. As checkboxes, they show up as work items that task-checker will tick. That can produce the "only checks boxes" commit the project rules forbid, and it makes the markers harder to recognise as commit points. Where the markers sit is fine: each comes after a tested point (2T, 3T, 4T), and 5C and 6C are correctly marked conditional. Only the format needs to change.

findings.title: Task 0 hard-codes `main` instead of using the configured target
findings.description: Task 0 expects `git.integration_branch` to be empty, stops if it isn't, and creates the branch with `git checkout -b ... main`. The git rules already cover a configured value: read it, call it the target, and fork from it. A clearer step would be: "Read the target (`cf config get git.integration_branch`, or `main` if empty), then create the branch from that target." This removes both the hard-coded branch name and the stop that no rule requires.

findings.title: No test for an unreadable file argument, and no command-level test for a template with no required headings
findings.description: The Functional Requirements list "unreadable" files and "a template with no required headings" as exit-2 cases. Task 3 implements the readability check in preflight. No test checks an unreadable file, for example one with `chmod 000`. The no-required-headings case is only tested in core (3T), not through the CLI exit-2 path (4T). The design only requires the valid-then-missing test, so neither gap is a hard failure. A one-line unreadable-file case in 3T would cover the last untested preflight branch.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage is complete
findings.description:
- PASS on existing designs: Task 4T (several real designs) and Task 5 (parity sweep).
- Missing-heading output and exit 1: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- docType failure: Tasks 3T and 4T, including the lenient quoted form.
- Ordered multi-file runs: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- Exit 2 with empty stdout in human and JSON mode, including valid-then-missing and the `cf guides update` message: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- JSON contract: Task 4T.
- Worktree-aware template: Task 4T, via the JSON `template` field.
- Unit normalization cases, all listed: Task 2T.
- Real-template check with `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough`: Task 3T.
- Build, lint, full suite and file sizes: Task 6.
- Guide-replacement readiness: Task 5 parity sweep.

findings.title: No scope creep; proportionate breakdown
findings.description: Every task traces to the design's Components or Development Approach, and Task 6's README check comes from design step 5. The extra 2T cases (`#hashtag`, template order) are cheap and protect the stated contract. There are three test files for three new source files, with no excess test tasks. The slice states no NFR, so no load-test or CI-gating task is needed.

findings.title: Sequencing and the test-with pattern are correct
findings.description: The sequence runs constant → pure validator → file layer → CLI → parity sweep → docs and full validation, and each step only uses earlier ones. Tasks 2T, 3T and 4T each come right after their implementation task. Every success line can be checked by a command (`pnpm -r build`, the package-filtered tests, `--help`), so a junior agent can complete each task without guessing.
